**CONFIDENTIAL — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Ownership, Indy Roof & Restoration
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**DATE:** May 14, 2025
**RE:** 90-Day Offensive Strategy — Taking Market Share from Raptor Roofing

---

**SITUATION BRIEF**

We hold 2,195 reviews at 4.9 stars. Raptor holds 671 at 5.0. On paper, they have a star-rating edge. In volume — the metric that drives LSA rank, consumer trust, and market perception — we dominate them by more than 3-to-1. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by star rating and the number of reviews.

 That asymmetry is our most powerful weapon and we are not using it aggressively enough. Here is how we change that this quarter.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Single-Channel Lead Dependency**

Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop. 

The contractors getting crushed right now all have the same profile: they built their entire lead generation around one paid channel. When that channel gets more expensive and less effective, they have nowhere to go except spend more.

 

Roofing LSA costs now run $55–$90 per lead, with storm damage queries hitting $150 or more in active weather zones.

 **Raptor is renting leads from Google. We need to make that rent feel unbearable by owning the organic and earned channels they are ignoring.**

**Weakness 2: Thin Geographic Roots Outside Center Grove and Greenwood**

Raptor has deliberately concentrated its community identity in Greenwood and Center Grove. That is smart micro-positioning — but it is also a ceiling. It leaves Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Avon, Brownsburg, and Mooresville comparatively uncontested from their brand. Their own website lists these markets but offers no localized content, no neighborhood-specific proof, no community ties. **Their brand identity is geographically narrow. We can establish dominant local presence in six surrounding submarkets before they react.**

**Weakness 3: A 5.0 Rating Is a Trap — And Their Volume Gap Is Catastrophic**

671 reviews is a thin foundation for a "premium" brand claim in a metro of two million people. A 5.0 with 671 reviews statistically signals a brand that is either early-stage or one that aggressively manages negative reviews out of public view. 

91% of homeowners rely on online reviews before choosing a contractor.

 When a homeowner compares Raptor's 671 reviews to our 2,195, the psychological authority gap is irreversible at the point of decision. **We must make that comparison unavoidable in our ad creative and landing pages.** Additionally, Raptor's brand "accountability" messaging has no third-party verification layer — no GuildQuality profile with external data, no volume of cross-platform reviews. Our depth of proof across platforms is superior; we are simply not weaponizing it.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE 90-DAY CAMPAIGNS**

**Campaign 1: "2,000+ Reasons" — Volume Dominance Ad Blitz**

Launch a Google Ads and Meta campaign directly targeting Greenwood, Center Grove, Carmel, and Fishers zip codes with a single creative hook: **"2,000+ families in Central Indiana trusted us with their roof. See why."** The ad links to neighborhood-specific landing pages showing real job photos, real homeowner names, and review counts by zip code. This is not a comparison ad — it does not name Raptor. It simply makes our social proof so visible and localized that Raptor's numbers look thin by comparison. Run Performance Max alongside standard search to capture the full funnel. 

Maximize the Google Business Profile with weekly updates, real job photos, accurate service listings, and every review responded to within 24 hours. Businesses with active GBPs saw 28% more discovery search views within 90 days.



**Campaign 2: Nextdoor + Neighborhood Facebook Group Infiltration in Center Grove and Greenwood**

This is their home turf. We take it. Assign two dedicated field marketers to saturate Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor with genuine project posts — before/after photos, real customer names, hyperlocal testimonials. Simultaneously, run Nextdoor Neighborhood Ads in these exact zip codes. 

By targeting specific neighborhoods, especially those where you are already working, you create geographic relevance and social proof. Unlike shared leads from third-party providers, you are not competing with multiple other roofers for the same prospect.

 Every crew truck in those neighborhoods gets a door hanger dropped on adjacent homes. Cost per lead for this channel is a fraction of LSA. **We do not need to outspend Raptor in their backyard. We need to out-show them.**

**Campaign 3: AI Search and GBP Domination Play**

Raptor's website content is thin on educational depth. Ours needs to be the resource Google AI and ChatGPT cite when homeowners ask about Indianapolis roofing. Immediately commission 12 location-specific blog articles targeting: "best roofers in Carmel IN," "hail damage roof claim Greenwood IN," "how long does a roof replacement take in Indianapolis," and equivalent queries for every submarket Raptor claims but doesn't own. 

When ChatGPT or Google AI Mode recommends a contractor, it pulls from websites that answer real questions. "How much does a furnace replacement cost in Charlotte?" beats "We provide quality HVAC service" every single time.

 Pair this with a dedicated Google Business Profile posting schedule — one post every three days, every post geotagged, every post with a real job photo.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a hyper-targeted LSA and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on Raptor's branded adjacent keywords — "Raptor Roofing reviews," "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis," "Raptor Roofing vs" — and route that traffic to a landing page titled: "Comparing Indianapolis Roofers? Here's What 2,195 Reviews Look Like."**

The page shows no competitor names. It shows our review volume, our cross-platform presence, our years in market since 2018, our BBB A+ standing, and a side-by-side of what 671 reviews versus 2,195 reviews actually means in terms of completed jobs and homeowner confidence. 

There is a fixed number of LSA leads in every roofing market, influenced by demand, seasonality, and competition.

 Every lead we intercept from a homeowner researching Raptor is a lead that costs Raptor money — they paid to generate that consumer's awareness, and we convert it.

**Cameron should be uncomfortable not because we are attacking his brand. He should be uncomfortable because we are making his review gap the centerpiece of every homeowner's decision — and he cannot fix 671 versus 2,195 in 90 days.**

This is where we win.

---

*Prepared for internal strategic use only. Recommend immediate budget alignment meeting within 5 business days.*

**Launch a "Insurance Coverage Audit" lead magnet this week targeting the 2005-2015 housing stock in Greenwood and Center Grove, before SPG turns its Roofing Contractor #92 ranking into paid creative.**

SPG just got a national third-party credential they can wave around (#92 on the 2025 Top 100, up from #128). Trying to out-credential them is a losing game we don't need to play this quarter. The asymmetric counter is to own the single highest-intent conversation no one in this market is having at scale: the RCV-to-ACV cliff and the RPS endorsements insurers are quietly slipping into renewals on roofs as young as 10 years. Greenwood and Center Grove housing stock is sitting right in the 10-20 year sweet spot, which means tens of thousands of homeowners in our service area are about to discover their policy pays half of what they think it does — and the contractor who tells them first wins the relationship before there's even a storm.

Execution this week: build a one-page offer ("Free 15-Minute Insurance Coverage Check — we read your declarations page and inspect your roof, no obligation"), wire it to a dedicated landing page with a Calendly slot, and push it through three channels by Friday: (1) a $1,500 geofenced Meta campaign targeting homeowners 35+ in the 46142/46143/46143 ZIPs, (2) a door-hanger drop on 500 homes in two target subdivisions with the RPS one-pager attached, and (3) an email to the past-customer list asking them to forward to neighbors. The script for reps is the moat — one hour of training, one laminated cheat sheet covering RCV vs ACV vs RPS, percentage-based deductibles. Most competitors are not having this conversation; SPG, Bone Dry, and Amos are still selling shingles.

Success metric this week: 25 booked coverage-check appointments and 8 inspections completed. Track close rate separately — these should run hotter than cold leads because we're showing up as an advocate, not a vendor.

---

**Deploy review-request automation across SMS and email tied to job completion, with a goal of closing the velocity gap on Indy Roof & Restoration (+76/30d) and Amos (+99/30d) within 90 days.**

Here's the uncomfortable number: at +17 reviews in the last 30 days, we are being out-paced 4-to-1 by Amos and 4.5-to-1 by Indy Roof in raw review velocity. Our 5.0 average is the prettiest in the top 10, but Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode are now surfacing one to three businesses by name, and the Roofing Webmasters data shows multi-platform review presence is the single strongest correlator with AI citation. We are leaving citations on the table every week we don't compound. Worse, Indy Roof just published a self-serving "Top 10 Roofing Companies in Indianapolis for 2026" listicle ranking themselves #1 on the strength of their review volume — that's the exact ammo AI systems will scrape and cite.

Execution this week: stand up a review request automation in whatever CRM/comms stack we're already running (NiceJob, Podium, BirdEye, or even just a Zapier-to-Twilio build if budget is tight — under $400/month either way). Trigger: job marked complete in the field. Sequence: SMS at 2 hours post-completion with a direct Google review link, email at 24 hours with the same link plus Facebook and Yelp options, second SMS at 72 hours only if no review posted. Audit Yelp and Facebook profiles in parallel — if either has under 50 reviews, route 30% of the asks there instead of Google to thicken the multi-platform footprint AI is rewarding.

Success metric: hit +30 Google reviews in the next 30 days (nearly doubling current velocity) and add a minimum of 15 reviews split across Yelp and Facebook in the same window. The compounding math gets us past Trojan and Richmond on volume by end of Q2 while widening the quality gap.

---

**Sign a hyperlocal community-anchor partnership this week that Bone Dry's 17-location footprint can never authentically match.**

Bone Dry is a real long-term threat — 30 years of brand recall in this market, 2,400+ reviews on the main location, Owens Corning Platinum and CertainTeed ShingleMaster both. We don't out-spend them on awareness. We out-local them. Bone Dry is headquartered in Indy but operates Colorado to Florida; they cannot credibly be "Greenwood's roofer" no matter how much they spend, and that's the gap to exploit while we're still small enough to be specific.

Execution this week: lock in one anchor partnership in Greenwood or Center Grove that puts the Raptor name in front of homeowners in a non-advertising context. Three candidates to pursue by Friday: (1) title sponsor for Greenwood Freedom Festival or the next Center Grove HS athletic season — even a $5K-$10K commitment gets logo placement and PA reads to thousands of exactly our demo, (2) a co-branded "free roof check before winter" event with a respected local insurance broker who is also seeing the ACV/RPS issue blow up at claim time and wants an honest contractor to refer to, or (3) a standing relationship with two or three top-producing Johnson County realtors to be their default pre-listing roof inspection contractor (free 10-minute inspections in exchange for being the recommended roofer at closing). Option 2 is the highest-leverage because it directly compounds the insurance-audit play in Action 1.

Success metric this week: one signed partnership agreement (verbal commitment + follow-up email is fine) and a calendar date for the first joint touchpoint within 30 days. Measure downstream by tagged lead source over the following 90 days — target 15 partnership-sourced leads in Q2.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**7301 E 46th St, Indianapolis, IN 46226 | [amosexteriors.com](https://www.amosexteriors.com)**
*Refreshed: Tuesday, May 20, 2025*

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company serving homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated since 1971, they hold GAF Master Elite Contractor status and maintain an A+ rating with the BBB, along with memberships in the NRCA and Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They now operate locations in both Indianapolis and Lafayette, IN,

 and their service line extends well beyond roofing — encompassing siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, and commercial exteriors — making them a full-envelope competitor, not just a roofing shop.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach estimates approximately 57 employees and $28.6 million in annual revenue

 (**confidence: low** — third-party modeled data). 

Prospeo pegs headcount at 51–100 employees

 with a separate revenue estimate of $12M. The wide spread between data sources ($12M–$28.6M) is typical for a company this size that doesn't publish financials. The most operationally meaningful data point: 

Amos received an SBA PPP loan of $584,200, retaining 40 jobs,

 which suggests a W-2 headcount floor of ~40 at time of application. 

Their sales department alone is reportedly led by a Director of Sales and includes 21 employees,

 signaling a heavily sales-rep-forward staffing model. Revenue estimate: $15M–$22M. **Confidence: medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



ZoomInfo flags an active search for an Estimator and Project Manager

 in Indianapolis. 

Their careers page is actively recruiting Home Improvement Sales Consultants, with reps expected to run company-provided leads as well as generate their own referrals.

 The more strategically notable signal: 

ZipRecruiter shows a posting for a Team Lead, Field Marketing

 — meaning they are building out a canvassing infrastructure with supervisory structure, not just adding bodies. 

BBB lists a Director of Marketing (Bruce McClain) and a Marketing Manager (Jana Perrott)

 as named contacts, indicating an in-house marketing function that most competitors their size don't maintain. No digital marketing, SEO, or paid media specialist roles were publicly visible in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The Google/Yelp gap here is stark and exploitable. Amos carries 3,094 Google reviews at 4.9 stars but 

holds only a 2.5-star rating on Yelp

 across 

19 Yelp reviews

 — a classic review-funneling setup where satisfied customers are directed exclusively to Google and Yelp is left unmanaged. 

BBB accreditation dates to 9/19/1993

 with an A+ rating, and their BBB page is well-maintained with named contacts. 

Facebook shows 1,383 page likes with 23 talking about the page

 — thin engagement for a company this size, suggesting Facebook is used as a credibility placeholder, not an active community or paid media channel. No active Facebook Ad Library campaigns were surfaced in the search results. On Angi (formerly Angie's List), they hold multiple positive reviews and 

have won the Angie's List Super Service Award.



---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, WP Rocket, Open Graph, and Nginx

 — a WordPress build with basic on-page SEO tooling in place. They have built out a dense location and service-area page architecture: 

service area pages explicitly name Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Geist, Plainfield, Avon, Speedway, Broad Ripple, Greenwood, Franklin, Mooresville, Anderson, and Greenfield.

 This is aggressive local SEO page sprawl — they are hunting every suburb Cameron targets. However, 

their core tech stack runs on jQuery 1.11.1 and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that suggests slow page speed and poor Core Web Vitals, a compounding weakness as Google increasingly weights page experience. No evidence of structured data / schema markup beyond what Yoast auto-generates. No local press backlinks were surfaced. Their AEO posture is thin — no FAQ schema, no "best of" citations in local media, and no visible content designed to answer long-tail conversational queries.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Amos Exteriors is a credible AI citation candidate due to their review volume and 54-year operating history, but their generative engine visibility is structurally weak. Their website runs on aging infrastructure with minimal structured data, no evident third-party editorial coverage (local press, industry publications), and no content formatted for AI extraction. 

Brands are 6.5x more likely to be cited in AI answers through third-party sources than through their own domains,

 and 

domain authority signals — specifically external referring domains — correlate strongly with AI Overview appearances.

 Amos has neither. In manual review of AI-generated responses to prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis" or "top roofing contractor near Carmel Indiana," Amos surfaces due to raw review volume but is not consistently named first or described with specific differentiating language. Their 54-year history and GAF Master Elite status are the two attributes most likely to pull AI citations if they were properly marked up and echoed in third-party sources — they are not doing this deliberately.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,094 vs. 673), brand age and legacy trust signals, broader service line (windows, doors, masonry, painting, commercial), dedicated in-house marketing staff, and a multi-location footprint now extending to Lafayette. **Where Raptor beats Amos:** Perfect 5.0 rating vs. 4.9 (meaningful in AI ranking logic and conversion psychology); zero accountability-outsourcing in the service model vs. Amos's canvasser-driven, high-volume sales rep structure that [per Indeed reviews] sends reps on unqualified 1.5-hour-drive leads; and a cleaner, more premium brand identity vs. Amos's volume-market positioning. **Most exploitable weakness:** 

Inside reviews describe leads that are "usually long drives" with reps traveling 1.5 hours each way for unqualified appointments, and canvassers setting appointments where homeowners "either don't know you're coming or don't understand why you're there"

 — a sales ops and customer experience problem that Raptor's high-touch, accountable model directly counters in the market.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **Dedicated location/service-area page architecture.** Amos has a page for nearly every suburb in central Indiana targeting "[City] + roofing" queries. Raptor should build equivalent depth — specifically for Carmel, Fishers, Zionsville, Noblesville, and Greenwood — with city-specific content, project photos, and schema markup that Amos is not executing properly. Do it cleaner and faster.

2. **Named marketing leadership as a credibility signal.** 

Amos lists a Director of Marketing and a Marketing Manager by name on their BBB profile.

 This is a small but real trust signal in B2C home services. Cameron should ensure Raptor's BBB and Google Business profiles list marketing/leadership contacts and use that visibility to create content authority (op-eds, local press quotes, home improvement columns) that Amos is not generating.

3. **Field marketing team-lead structure.** The Team Lead, Field Marketing posting on ZipRecruiter signals Amos is scaling a structured canvassing operation with management hierarchy. Watch whether this translates into heavier presence at Lowes/Home Depot parking lot events, HOA outreach, or neighborhood drop campaigns in Raptor's core zip codes — and prepare a counter-program that emphasizes Raptor's referral-first, non-canvassing reputation as a premium differentiator.

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 20 businesses in eight states, including 11 Midwest locations plus Bone Dry Roofing West, Florida, Commercial, Roof One, QRS, Ravlin's, RCV, and Gary's Roofing

Of the $121M reported in 2022, approximately $36 million (30%) came from the Indianapolis office alone.

 **Revenue confidence: medium** — the Indianapolis location is likely a $40-50M+ operation on its own by 2025 based on trajectory.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active and broad.

 Roles posted on ZipRecruiter and Indeed include:

; 

Systems Analyst for business operations, noted as being in "growth mode"

;

; and 

Home Solution Specialists (in-home sales reps) and Commercial Service Technicians.

 The Systems Analyst and Division Manager postings are the ones to watch — ops-level builds like that precede market expansion pushes. No standalone marketing coordinator or CMO-level hire is currently visible in Indiana, which tracks with their in-house CMO (Matt Tyner) being tenured.

## 4. Off-Google Presence



On Yelp, the Indianapolis location at 7735 Winton Dr has 75 reviews

 — versus 2,422 on Google. That is a 97% review-funneling gap, the clearest sign in this market of a team that has mastered Google review capture but has done nothing to cultivate Yelp. Their Facebook presence (

825 likes, 264 people talking about it

) is active but thin for a company of their scale. The UTM parameters in their Facebook profile links (`utm_campaign=profile-link&campaign_code=BDR-DIG-ORGS-ROOF-IN-PHO-FB-202402`) show they are tracking social-to-web traffic with some discipline.

 that generates community goodwill mentions. BBB complaints page is live but complaint volume is not alarming based on available data. No notable Reddit presence identified for the Indy location.

Bone Dry operates `bonedry.com` with a dedicated subdirectory at `bonedry.com/indianapolis/` and location-specific service pages (e.g., `bonedry.com/indianapolis/roofing/`).

 — a competent but not cutting-edge setup. Their multi-location architecture gives them a domain authority advantage that a single-location operator cannot easily replicate; `bonedry.com` almost certainly carries a DA of 45+ based on press coverage, Owens Corning partner links, and the [2023 Roofing Contractor Magazine profile](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing). AEO posture is not differentiated — no visible FAQ schema, no structured "ask" content targeting voice or AI-surfaced queries.

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry Roofing is almost certainly named in AI answers for broad Indianapolis roofing queries. The combination of their volume (2,422 Google reviews), national press coverage (Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Contractor of the Year), multi-state footprint, and aged domain makes them a high-probability citation for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis" or "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Their BBB A+ status and F.C. Tucker partnership (

Bone Dry is a member of F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

) generate structured third-party mentions that LLMs index heavily. **Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Updated: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Erie Home, founded in 1982 and headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, is a leading direct-to-consumer residential re-roofing platform operating across North America.

 

Pat Trompeter is the company's founder (now Chairman of the Board), with Jenilee Common serving as CEO and Randy Hamilton as President.

 Their differentiator is a fully vertically integrated model — 

Erie handles the end-to-end process from lead generation through final installation, positioning themselves on the peace-of-mind pitch rather than local craftsmanship.

 Critically, 

as of September 8, 2025, Erie Home was acquired by Leaf Home

, folding it into the largest DTC residential home services platform in North America — a post-acquisition integration dynamic that should be front of mind for Raptor.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



Erie Home ranked #4 on Roofing Contractor's 2025 Top 100 list with reported annual revenue of $609 million in 2024.

 For headcount,

 — suggesting a workforce north of 3,000–5,000 FTEs nationally. **Confidence: Medium** (no hard FTE figure publicly confirmed post-acquisition). The Indianapolis location is one branch of a national machine; local decision-making authority is limited.

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



Erie Home's active Indeed posting for Indianapolis lists roofing subcontractors, noting the company has been ranked in the Top 10 on the Qualified Remodeler Top 500 list for consecutive years.

 

ZipRecruiter shows multiple "Hiring Immediately for Roofing Subcontractors" listings — Erie is actively seeking crews for consistent, year-round work.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or branch management postings were identified for Indianapolis specifically in the last 30 days. The subcontractor-heavy hiring posture confirms Erie does not self-perform installs locally — a meaningful accountability gap Raptor can exploit.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

Erie's Indianapolis Google profile sits at 277 reviews / 4.6 stars with **zero reviews in the last 90 days and no owner responses on record** — a dead profile for a company this size. This is not organic momentum; it reads as a centrally managed, now-neglected local GBP. 

Erie claims an A+ BBB rating nationally

, but the BBB profile is managed from Toledo — there is no Indianapolis-specific BBB entity. 

Consumer Affairs reviews nationally include complaints about leaking roofs post-installation and improper ridge vent installation

 — the kind of execution failures consistent with a subcontractor-dependent model. 

LinkedIn marketing copy touts "outstanding ratings across all major review sites including Google, BBB, GuildQuality, TrustPilot, Birdeye, Indeed and Glassdoor"

 — but the Indianapolis Google stagnation tells a different story. No active Facebook Ad Library presence was confirmed for the Indianapolis market specifically at time of this brief.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

[eriehome.com](https://eriehome.com) is a nationally scaled domain with substantial authority derived from press coverage of the Leaf Home acquisition, Roofing Contractor Top 100 citations, and PR wire syndication. The Indianapolis location page ([eriehome.com/locations/roofing/indianapolis-in/](https://eriehome.com/locations/roofing/indianapolis-in/)) is templated and thin. 

It targets Indianapolis, Carmel, Greenwood, and Lawrence in copy

 but reads like a scaled location page, not locally authored content. 

The site's HTML is 154.96 KB — more than 4x the average — which can negatively impact load times and user experience.

 No evidence of a local Indianapolis blog content strategy or backlinks from Indy-specific media (IBJ, IndyStar, Indy Chamber). Their AEO posture nationally is strong due to brand volume, but locally they are invisible in terms of schema-rich, city-specific content that would drive AI citation.

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Erie Home, due to sheer national revenue scale ($609M, Top 5 nationally) and the high-profile Leaf Home acquisition press coverage, is likely cited in generic "largest roofing companies" AI answers. However, for hyper-local queries like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," or "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville," Erie's thin, templated location pages provide weak AEO signals. AI engines favor locally specific, structured, review-rich content — Raptor's 673 reviews at 5.0 stars, combined with locally authored content targeting those exact suburb queries, represents a direct opportunity to outrank Erie in generative engine responses for Central Indiana. Erie's post-acquisition integration noise is also likely suppressing any new AEO content investment at the local level right now.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Erie beats Raptor:** National brand recognition, a lifetime warranty product, third-party financing at scale, and a $609M revenue machine that can spend on paid media without flinching. Their workaterie.com recruitment engine and Sales MIT program means they can flood local markets with commission-driven reps quickly.

**Where Raptor beats Erie:** Raptor holds a 5.0 star rating at 673 reviews vs Erie's 4.6 at 277 with zero recent review velocity — a dead signal in Google's local algorithm. Erie's subcontractor installation model is its most exploitable weakness: 

Erie is a "one call close" company where reps must convince homeowners to pay 3–4x what they expected for a product they did not ask about

 — the exact opposite of Raptor's accountability positioning. The most exploitable weakness: **zero owner responses on the Indianapolis GBP in any recorded window** — Cameron can weaponize this contrast in sales conversations and review strategy immediately.

Cameron should build a direct comparison into sales scripts and proposal decks: Raptor uses its own crews, Erie uses subcontractors. Make it a documented close, not just a verbal point.

2. **Lifetime warranty language.** 

Erie's CEO pitch is "we will be with you for the rest of the life of the roof and the next one."

 That is a powerful retention and close narrative. Evaluate whether Raptor's warranty language is as visceral and forward-looking in collateral.

3. **Monitor the Leaf Home integration for local service degradation.** 

The September 2025 Leaf Home acquisition combined two DTC leaders into one entity

 — integrations of this scale historically cause local customer service gaps, slower lead response, and review stagnation (which is already showing in Indy). Set a Google Alerts cadence for "Erie Home Indianapolis" and "Leaf Home Indianapolis" and be ready to surge Raptor's local paid media when Erie's GBP rating starts slipping.

## 2. Tactic of the Week

### Pitch a Local News Outlet This Week for a Storm-Season Roofing Cost Story

**The Why**



Modern algorithms prioritize relevance and intent, making one link from a local home builders association or regional news outlet carry far more weight than dozens of links from spammy directories.

 Raptor's estimated ~15 referring domains versus Bone Dry's estimated ~130 is the widest performance gap on the entire dashboard. The fastest single move to close that gap is earning one high-authority local press backlink — not a paid ad placement, a byline. The mechanism is straightforward: a dofollow editorial link from an Indianapolis Business Journal, Indianapolis Star, or WTHR.com story carries domain authority in the 55-70 range. 

With the emergence of AI, brand mentions and backlinks signal that your roofing business is credible, active, and trusted by the community

 — which means the same coverage that earns a backlink also seeds the named-entity data that Perplexity, Google AI Overview, and ChatGPT draw on when constructing their recommended-contractor lists.

The timing is perfect. 

The national average roof replacement now costs $19,800, and homeowners are getting sticker shock and asking AI to find the best roofer.

 Every local reporter covering consumer spending is looking for a credentialed local contractor who can explain why roofing costs jumped and what homeowners should do right now. You are that source.

**The How**

1. Write a 150-word expert pitch today — not a press release. Address it to the consumer or business reporter at IBJ, Indianapolis Star, and WTHR's digital desk by name. Subject line: "Local roofer: here's why your next roof costs $4K more than last year, and what Indy homeowners should ask before signing anything."

2. In the pitch, offer three specific data points: (a) the material cost increase due to shingle manufacturer price hikes, (b) one or two hyperlocal hail events from the 2025 season that drove demand, and (c) a "three questions every homeowner should ask a roofer before getting an estimate" hook — the kind of utility content editors can turn into a listicle or sidebar.

3. Offer a 20-minute phone interview, a job-site photo opportunity, and a quote for attribution. Propose that Raptor Roofing be identified by name and city in the piece.

4. If the reporter bites, confirm in your follow-up that the company website URL (raptorroofing.com) is included in the online version of the story. That URL is the backlink. Do not accept print-only placement; the digital placement is the SEO asset.

5. If IBJ or the Star passes, escalate to Angie's List editorial (DA 75+) or NARI Indianapolis chapter news, both of which accept contractor-sourced expert commentary. 

Roofing companies can earn backlinks by publishing helpful guides, supporting community events, joining trade organizations, sharing project stories, and building partnerships.



**Success Metric — 30 days**

Track in Google Search Console: organic impressions for "Indianapolis roof replacement cost" and "Indianapolis roofer" queries. Baseline them this week before the placement runs. One mid-DA editorial link typically produces a measurable impressions lift within 21-30 days in a market this size. The aggregator and AI-adjacent surfaces surfaced in these searches (RoofersUp, Angi, Yelp, FindTrustedRoofers) return Bone Dry Roofing and Indy Roof & Restoration consistently across Indianapolis-adjacent suburbs. Raptor appears on FindTrustedRoofers.com with a 5.0 / 533 reviews notation,

 — but this listing does not surface in the AI-generated answer layers tested. Raptor was not cited by name in any AI Overview or Perplexity-style answer card for any of the six suburb-specific queries.

### Is Raptor Cited?

Based on this week's search scan: Raptor is absent from AI-generated answer surfaces for all six tested queries. It appears in directory listings (FindTrustedRoofers, BBB) but those listings are not being pulled into the citation layer of Google AI Overview or equivalent. The distinction matters: being in a directory is passive; being cited by name in an AI answer requires that the source feeding the AI model treats Raptor as a named, authoritative entity — which requires press coverage, editorial mentions, or a schema-rich page that AI crawlers can confidently parse.

**1. Named-entity press coverage — the most critical gap.** 

AI engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity pull data from trusted sources to determine which roofing companies to recommend, and AI rewards companies with consistent, real-world proof across every platform.

 Bone Dry has Roofing Contractor Magazine. Indy Roof has local TV and Habitat for Humanity coverage.  Raptor lists service cities in footer text only. There is no dedicated, content-bearing page for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, or Zionsville — meaning when a user asks "best roofer Fishers Indiana," there is no Raptor URL for the AI to cite.

**CONFIDENTIAL — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Ownership, Indy Roof & Restoration
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**DATE:** May 14, 2025
**RE:** 90-Day Offensive Strategy — Taking Market Share from Raptor Roofing

---

**SITUATION BRIEF**

We hold 2,195 reviews at 4.9 stars. Raptor holds 671 at 5.0. On paper, they have a star-rating edge. In volume — the metric that drives LSA rank, consumer trust, and market perception — we dominate them by more than 3-to-1. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by star rating and the number of reviews.

 That asymmetry is our most powerful weapon and we are not using it aggressively enough. Here is how we change that this quarter.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Single-Channel Lead Dependency**

Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop. 

The contractors getting crushed right now all have the same profile: they built their entire lead generation around one paid channel. When that channel gets more expensive and less effective, they have nowhere to go except spend more.

 

Roofing LSA costs now run $55–$90 per lead, with storm damage queries hitting $150 or more in active weather zones.

 **Raptor is renting leads from Google. We need to make that rent feel unbearable by owning the organic and earned channels they are ignoring.**

**Weakness 2: Thin Geographic Roots Outside Center Grove and Greenwood**

Raptor has deliberately concentrated its community identity in Greenwood and Center Grove. That is smart micro-positioning — but it is also a ceiling. It leaves Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Avon, Brownsburg, and Mooresville comparatively uncontested from their brand. Their own website lists these markets but offers no localized content, no neighborhood-specific proof, no community ties. **Their brand identity is geographically narrow. We can establish dominant local presence in six surrounding submarkets before they react.**

**Weakness 3: A 5.0 Rating Is a Trap — And Their Volume Gap Is Catastrophic**

671 reviews is a thin foundation for a "premium" brand claim in a metro of two million people. A 5.0 with 671 reviews statistically signals a brand that is either early-stage or one that aggressively manages negative reviews out of public view. 

91% of homeowners rely on online reviews before choosing a contractor.

 When a homeowner compares Raptor's 671 reviews to our 2,195, the psychological authority gap is irreversible at the point of decision. **We must make that comparison unavoidable in our ad creative and landing pages.** Additionally, Raptor's brand "accountability" messaging has no third-party verification layer — no GuildQuality profile with external data, no volume of cross-platform reviews. Our depth of proof across platforms is superior; we are simply not weaponizing it.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE 90-DAY CAMPAIGNS**

**Campaign 1: "2,000+ Reasons" — Volume Dominance Ad Blitz**

Launch a Google Ads and Meta campaign directly targeting Greenwood, Center Grove, Carmel, and Fishers zip codes with a single creative hook: **"2,000+ families in Central Indiana trusted us with their roof. See why."** The ad links to neighborhood-specific landing pages showing real job photos, real homeowner names, and review counts by zip code. This is not a comparison ad — it does not name Raptor. It simply makes our social proof so visible and localized that Raptor's numbers look thin by comparison. Run Performance Max alongside standard search to capture the full funnel. 

Maximize the Google Business Profile with weekly updates, real job photos, accurate service listings, and every review responded to within 24 hours. Businesses with active GBPs saw 28% more discovery search views within 90 days.



**Campaign 2: Nextdoor + Neighborhood Facebook Group Infiltration in Center Grove and Greenwood**

This is their home turf. We take it. Assign two dedicated field marketers to saturate Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor with genuine project posts — before/after photos, real customer names, hyperlocal testimonials. Simultaneously, run Nextdoor Neighborhood Ads in these exact zip codes. 

By targeting specific neighborhoods, especially those where you are already working, you create geographic relevance and social proof. Unlike shared leads from third-party providers, you are not competing with multiple other roofers for the same prospect.

 Every crew truck in those neighborhoods gets a door hanger dropped on adjacent homes. Cost per lead for this channel is a fraction of LSA. **We do not need to outspend Raptor in their backyard. We need to out-show them.**

**Campaign 3: AI Search and GBP Domination Play**

Raptor's website content is thin on educational depth. Ours needs to be the resource Google AI and ChatGPT cite when homeowners ask about Indianapolis roofing. Immediately commission 12 location-specific blog articles targeting: "best roofers in Carmel IN," "hail damage roof claim Greenwood IN," "how long does a roof replacement take in Indianapolis," and equivalent queries for every submarket Raptor claims but doesn't own. 

When ChatGPT or Google AI Mode recommends a contractor, it pulls from websites that answer real questions. "How much does a furnace replacement cost in Charlotte?" beats "We provide quality HVAC service" every single time.

 Pair this with a dedicated Google Business Profile posting schedule — one post every three days, every post geotagged, every post with a real job photo.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a hyper-targeted LSA and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on Raptor's branded adjacent keywords — "Raptor Roofing reviews," "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis," "Raptor Roofing vs" — and route that traffic to a landing page titled: "Comparing Indianapolis Roofers? Here's What 2,195 Reviews Look Like."**

The page shows no competitor names. It shows our review volume, our cross-platform presence, our years in market since 2018, our BBB A+ standing, and a side-by-side of what 671 reviews versus 2,195 reviews actually means in terms of completed jobs and homeowner confidence. 

There is a fixed number of LSA leads in every roofing market, influenced by demand, seasonality, and competition.

 Every lead we intercept from a homeowner researching Raptor is a lead that costs Raptor money — they paid to generate that consumer's awareness, and we convert it.

**Cameron should be uncomfortable not because we are attacking his brand. He should be uncomfortable because we are making his review gap the centerpiece of every homeowner's decision — and he cannot fix 671 versus 2,195 in 90 days.**

This is where we win.

---

*Prepared for internal strategic use only. Recommend immediate budget alignment meeting within 5 business days.*

Success metric: two signed-up agent partners by end of next week, three coverage audits booked through agent referral within 30 days. ## 4. Off-Google Presence

AI models process content in digestible sections (150–300 words with clear subheadings), and sites structured this way improve their chances of appearing in AI answers and featured snippets.

 Raptor's current city pages use long unbroken text blocks that are not chunked for AI extraction. 

FAQ schema specifically tells Google a page contains authoritative answers to common questions, and when used correctly it can improve click-through rates 20–30% and qualify a page for AI-generated answer cards in tools like Perplexity or ChatGPT.

### Implement RoofingContractor + FAQPage Schema on Every Suburb Service Page — Today

AI engines — Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, ChatGPT with Browse — do not guess at what your business does or where it operates.

 For Raptor, "skipping" is the operative word: zero named citations in the six AI-style queries tested this week. The structural reason is almost certainly missing or incomplete structured data combined with a thin review count. Schema is the half you can fix in 48 hours.

Benefits include improved search result appearance via rich snippets, better local search rankings, and increased AI citation likelihood.





Clear NAP and hours in schema reduce mismatches and help map visibility. As answer engines pull factual data directly, structured data boosts your chances of being cited or synthesized in AI responses.

**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**
**TO:** Ownership, Bone Dry Roofing (Indianapolis)
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**RE:** 90-Day Market Share Campaign Against Raptor Roofing
**DATE:** May 21, 2026

---

**SITUATION SUMMARY**

We have 954 Google reviews at 4.9 stars. 

Bone Dry Roofing's Indianapolis office is the headquarters of our business, which spans nine total offices across five states.

 

We were named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by Roofing Contractor Magazine.

 Raptor has momentum in specific southern suburban corridors. We have the institutional size, credentialing, and review volume to end that momentum. Here is exactly how.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: They are a small, geographically concentrated operation with no institutional depth.**



Raptor Roofing has been serving the Indianapolis area only since 2016.

 Nine years in a market where we have operated since 1989 is a resume gap, not a credential. Their brand is built around two named personalities — 

locals Cameron Blakely and Patrick Kinney

 — which is a fragile foundation. One bad hire, one capacity crunch during a storm event, and the "family accountability" message collapses in real time. **We should force that capacity issue by outbidding them on volume during the next storm cycle.**

**Weakness 2: Their lead sources are entirely Google-dependent and therefore bidable.**

Raptor's known primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — channels where we can compete dollar for dollar and win on review volume alone. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by your star rating and the number of reviews.

 We have 279 more reviews than Raptor and a 4.9 star rating. 

LSA ranking heavily favors review count and responsiveness, which means a small operator with 50 solid reviews can outrank a bigger company that doesn't respond fast

 — and the inverse is equally true. **We outrank them structurally on the LSA algorithm today. We simply need to fund it aggressively.** 

If our competitors have open budgets, Google feeds them first.

 We should set an uncapped weekly LSA budget and bury them at the top of the results page.

**Weakness 3: Their geographic identity is a ceiling, not a moat.**

Raptor has planted their flag specifically in Greenwood and Center Grove. This is tactically smart for a small operator, but strategically brittle. It makes them a neighborhood brand, not a metro brand. Meanwhile, 

in 2022, Bone Dry reported revenues of $121,633,676, ranking comfortably at No. 18 on Roofing Contractor Magazine's Top 100 list, with $36 million — around 30% — coming from our original Indianapolis office.

 We are a metro-scale operation being beaten in a suburb by a boutique. **That is an execution problem, not a brand problem.** We have the infrastructure to flood Greenwood and Center Grove with canvassers, yard signs, and neighborhood-specific digital ads in 30 days.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: LSA Dominance — "Out-Budget, Out-Rank, Out-Answer"**



2026 Google LSA cost per lead for roofing runs $50–$130.

 We raise our Indianapolis LSA weekly budget ceiling to a minimum of $2,500/week — no cap. We assign a dedicated phone responder whose sole job is answering LSA calls in under 90 seconds, seven days a week. 

Google tracks how fast you answer the phone. If you miss calls, your ad rank drops. If you answer in 3 rings, you move up.

 Raptor cannot match our review volume, cannot match our response infrastructure, and cannot match an open budget. We take the top LSA slot and hold it. Ad creative angle: "954 reviews. 4.9 stars. Indianapolis's most reviewed roofer. One call answered."

**Campaign 2: Center Grove / Greenwood Neighborhood Conquest — Direct Mail + Yard Sign Blitz**

We purchase a targeted mailing list of every homeowner in 46143 and 46142 ZIP codes with homes built between 1990–2010 — peak replacement age. We deploy a direct mail piece with the headline: **"Your neighbors chose Indianapolis's most-reviewed roofer. Here's why."** Back panel features 5 actual named customer testimonials from Johnson County. Simultaneously, we offer a $50 gift card incentive to any completed job customer in those ZIPs who posts a yard sign for 30 days. Goal: 200 yard signs in Raptor's home territory within 60 days. 

Our commitment to quality is reflected in having a production supervisor who remains on-site for the duration of every project, serving as the main point of contact — and per company policy, no payment is taken until the customer has expressed total agreement and satisfaction with the work.

 That is a warranty story Raptor cannot match. Put it on every door.

**Campaign 3: Meta + YouTube Conquest Ads — "35 Years vs. 9 Years"**

We run a geo-targeted Meta and YouTube pre-roll campaign across the full Indianapolis metro. Creative angle: a 30-second video. Open with: "When the storm hits, you want the company that's been here since before your roof was built." Show 1989 founding footage or imagery. Show our Owens Corning Platinum Preferred and CertainTeed ShingleMaster credentials — 

we are one of the few roofing companies in Indianapolis to hold the distinguished Platinum Preferred and ShingleMaster Select contractor status.

 Close with the review count. We do not name Raptor. We do not need to. Every homeowner in Center Grove who has seen Raptor's "local guys" ads will do the math themselves. Budget: $8,000/month for 90 days.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a dedicated "Greenwood/Center Grove" landing page and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on branded and near-branded Raptor keyword terms.**



PPC is a competitive bidding war for prime spots on Google. In the roofing niche, the cost per click is high, and conversion rate optimization is critical — with CPC ranging $5 to $25+ per click for high-intent keywords.

 We build a standalone landing page at bonedry.com/greenwood-roofing that loads in under 2 seconds, features Johnson County-specific testimonials, our 35-year history, and a prominent "Get a Free Estimate" form above the fold. We then bid on keywords including "Raptor Roofing alternative," "roofing Greenwood Indiana," "Center Grove roofing contractor," and "best roofing company Greenwood" with a dedicated $3,000/month budget. **Anyone in Greenwood who searches Raptor's name or their territory keywords sees us first, second, or third.** We do not need to say anything negative. We just need to be present, credentialed, and more reviewed every time a homeowner goes looking. That is the move that makes Cameron uncomfortable — because there is no counter to institutional size, 35 years of history, and a review count nearly 300 ahead of his.

**We have every structural advantage. The only thing missing is urgency. This memo is the starting gun.**

---
*Prepared for internal distribution only. Treat as competitive strategy — do not distribute externally.*

# Raptor Roofing — This Week's Moves

## 1. **Record a 90-second video answer for "What does the new ACV roof rule mean for my Indiana homeowners policy?" and ship it as the schema-marked answer block on a new Greenwood-specific FAQ page by Friday.**

The March 18 Fannie/Freddie ACV rule change is the single biggest insurance-coverage shift in residential roofing in years, and right now nobody in the Indianapolis top 10 has claimed the local educational answer. BrightLocal's data says 45% of consumers now use AI tools to find local services (up from 6% a year ago) and AI engines cite only 3-5 sources. The roofer who publishes the clearest, most-cited Indiana-specific ACV explainer in the next two weeks becomes the answer ChatGPT and Perplexity quote when a Greenwood homeowner asks what their insurance actually covers now. Stay Dry's self-ranked "Top 10" page proves competitors will fill content vacuums if we don't.

Execution: shoot the video on a kitchen table, owner on camera (this is the local-owner moat — no agency voice), transcribe it, structure the page as FAQ schema with 8-10 questions a real Greenwood homeowner would ask ("Will my mortgage company let me switch to ACV?", "What's the out-of-pocket gap on a $22K replacement?", "Is my current policy RCV or ACV?"). Publish under `/insurance/acv-rule-indiana/`. Add internal links from every storm-damage page already live.

Success metric this week: page indexed in Google Search Console, FAQ schema validated, and a baseline screenshot of where Raptor appears (or doesn't) when you type "what is ACV roof coverage Indiana" into ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. Re-test in 30 days. Secondary metric: sales team uses the URL as a leave-behind on every storm-damage estimate within 14 days.

## 2. **Counter-position 3 Kings' roof rejuvenation pitch with a "Rejuvenation vs. Replace: The Honest Answer" comparison page and arm the sales team with a one-page script by Thursday.**

3 Kings Roofing — veteran-owned, 5.0-star, serving Greenwood among 18 communities — pushed a press release on May 11 promoting roof rejuvenation as a differentiated service. That's a direct shot into our backyard from a company that matches our review rating. The trap is reacting by adding rejuvenation to our service menu; that's a margin-killer and dilutes the premium positioning. The better play is owning the educational high ground: be the roofer who explains, plainly, when rejuvenation is legitimate (10-12 year old roof, granule loss but intact deck, owner staying 3-5 more years) and when it's a band-aid that costs you money (any storm damage claim scenario, any roof past year 15, any sale-prep situation).

The page should name rejuvenation as a real product (don't dismiss it — that reads as defensive), then walk through three scenarios with photos showing what rejuvenation can and cannot fix. Close with: "If a contractor recommends rejuvenation on a roof with hail bruising or active leaks, get a second opinion." That sentence is the whole point — it inoculates every Greenwood homeowner 3 Kings talks to. Sales team gets a printed one-pager version to hand out when prospects mention they got a rejuvenation quote.

Success metric this week: page live, one-pager distributed to all sales reps, and a tracked phrase added to discovery calls — "Has anyone else quoted you on rejuvenation or coating?" — logged in CRM. Target: identify at least 3 deals in the next 30 days where a competitor (3 Kings or otherwise) pitched rejuvenation and we won on the comparison.

## 3. **Pitch IBJ, Indianapolis Monthly, and Center Grove Magazine this week for a "5.0 stars across 675 reviews" feature angle — the highest-rated high-volume roofer in Indianapolis — before Stay Dry's self-published Top 10 page calcifies as the canonical local answer.**

Stay Dry published their own "Updated 2026 Top 10 Roofing Companies in Indianapolis" ranking themselves #1, citing Inc. 5000 and BBB A+. That page is currently indexing for "best roofing companies Indianapolis 2026" and similar queries. We can't out-self-publish them credibly — but we have something they don't: a verifiable, mathematically defensible claim that no other top-10 Indianapolis roofer can make. Amos has 3,098 reviews at 4.9. Bone Dry has 2,422 at 4.8. Indy Roof has 2,207 at 4.9. Raptor is the only company in the top 10 by volume with a perfect 5.0 across 600+ reviews. That's not marketing language — it's arithmetic, and journalists love arithmetic.

The pitch angle: "How a 16-employee Greenwood roofer became the highest-rated high-volume contractor in Indianapolis." Lead with the data table. Offer the editor an exclusive on the owner-led, no-outsourced-accountability operating model. Three outlets, three custom pitches, sent by end of week. Also pitch Inside INdiana Business and the Greenwood Chamber newsletter as backups. A single earned-media placement linking back to Raptor.com is a stronger SEO and AEO signal than anything Stay Dry can self-author, and it gives the sales team a third-party credential to drop in every proposal.

Success metric this week: 5 pitches sent, 2 editor replies (even "not now" counts as relationship-opened), and the data table ("5.0 stars / 675 reviews — only top-10 Indianapolis roofer with a perfect average at this volume") added as a fixed module on the homepage and the about page by Friday regardless of whether press lands. The claim itself does work

**Raptor Roofing — Cameron Blakely, CMO Dashboard**

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they serve both residential and commercial customers as a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor, and hold memberships in good standing with the BBB (A+), the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They now operate with locations in both Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, making them a multi-market operator — a meaningful scale distinction from most Indy competitors. Their core differentiator is a full-service exterior platform: roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, and commercial painting all under one roof, with a heavy lean into insurance claims navigation.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach puts annual revenue at $28.6 million (2025 estimate) with 57 employees.

 

Prospeo independently estimates approximately 51–100 employees.

 **Confidence: medium.** Revenue figures from third-party data aggregators carry noise, but the $12M–$29M range across multiple sources is plausible for a 50+ year old multi-trade operation with a 3,000+ review velocity. 

A PPP loan of $584,200 from Stock Yards Bank resulted in the reported retention of 40 jobs

, which provides a floor on their W-2 headcount. 

Known leadership includes a Director of Sales, a VP of Construction (Todd Danbom), and a Marketing Director (Charles Crowley).



---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



ZipRecruiter shows an open Team Lead, Field Marketing role in Indianapolis.

 

Their own careers page is actively recruiting Home Improvement Sales Consultants, trained to "out-sell the competition," running both company-provided leads and self-generated referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags an open Estimator & Project Manager role in Indianapolis.

 The Field Marketing Team Lead posting is the one to watch — it signals they are expanding or restructuring canvassing operations, which is their dominant top-of-funnel model. A marketing specialist role was also recently active per Glassdoor. No C-suite or digital marketing director-level hires detected in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**



Amos Roofing & Exteriors holds only 2.5 stars on Yelp

 against their 4.9 on Google — a significant platform disparity that is a textbook review-funneling signal. They are clearly driving customers to Google and not managing Yelp proactively. 

Facebook shows 1,383 likes with only 23 people "talking about this"

 — minimal organic engagement for a company of their scale, suggesting Facebook is largely dormant. No active Facebook Ad Library presence was confirmed. 

BBB-accredited since September 1993

 with an A+ rating and active recent reviews. 

On Angi, they carry a 4.5 overall rating

 — solid but not perfect. GuildQuality shows verified reviews including some negative feedback around siding quality and communication, concentrated in 2017–2018 but visible in search.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Amos Exteriors runs on WordPress with PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — a legacy tech stack that likely limits Core Web Vitals performance and structured data execution. They have built out a deep location/service page architecture (e.g., [amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) which generates decent long-tail coverage across Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, and Greenwood. However, the jQuery 1.11.1 version is outdated by roughly a decade, which is a schema implementation and page speed liability. No evidence of a robust backlink strategy from local press or Indy-area publications. Their blog exists but content cadence appears irregular. The GAF Master Elite designation earns them a high-authority inbound link from [gaf.com](https://www.gaf.com/en-us/roofing-contractors/residential/usa/in/indianapolis/amos-exteriors-inc-1113337) which Raptor should match or counter.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current AI engine behavior for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," and "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville": Amos Exteriors is likely to appear in AI-generated answers by virtue of their review volume (3,098 Google reviews), domain age, multi-location page structure, and GAF Master Elite certification — all of which are strong citation signals for LLMs pulling from structured web data. Their 54-year operating history and BBB A+ accreditation since 1993 further boost entity authority in knowledge graph indexing. Raptor, with 675 reviews and a 5.0 rating, is a thinner entity profile at this stage. The gap is not about quality — it is about entity depth and crawlable citation surface area. Raptor should be building AEO-optimized FAQ schema, press mentions, and third-party citation anchors (NRCA membership, GAF certification page, local news features) to close this AI visibility gap.

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,098 vs. 675), domain age, multi-trade service breadth, Lafayette market expansion, and an in-house marketing department with named Director of Marketing and Marketing Manager on the BBB profile. Their insurance claims navigation operation is a well-oiled machine with dedicated reps named throughout reviews. **Where Raptor beats Amos:** Raptor holds a 5.0 vs. 4.9 — the cleanest rating in the Indy top 10 by volume — and runs a premium, accountable positioning that Amos cannot credibly claim given Glassdoor complaints about sales rep quality, canvassing no-shows, and a 2.5 Yelp rating.  — a trust and brand integrity gap Raptor can hammer directly in paid and social messaging.

Amos explicitly builds out named suburb service areas including Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Geist, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, Franklin, and Anderson

 with dedicated URLs. Raptor should audit whether it has comparable depth — each suburb page is an independent AEO and local SEO asset.

, and upsells into siding, gutters, windows, and masonry on the same job. Monitor whether their average ticket size is growing through multi-trade attachment — this is the revenue-per-customer lever Raptor should have an opinion on.

## 4. Off-Google Presence

BBB-accredited since July 2019 with an A+ rating

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

careers page

) suggests a standard local SEO landing page strategy.

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Indy Roof & Restoration does appear in AI-generated local roundups. The Stay Dry Roofing roundup — which itself ranks in Google for Indy roofing queries — 

identifies them specifically for insurance advocacy and 24/7 emergency response, and recommends them for homeowners wanting intense insurance-claim support and mitigation services.

 That content will be scraped by LLMs and surface in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini responses to queries like "best storm damage roofer Indianapolis." However, their own domain does not appear to have AEO-optimized content (FAQ schema, structured Q&A, cited statistics) that would make them a primary source in generative answers. **Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Refreshed: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 2022 by Cheryl Edens and Mitchel Dotson, originally built around Kevin Dotson — a veteran roofing salesman who had spent years at another local company before going out on his own at 60.

 

Indy Rooftops brands itself as a woman-owned business rooted in Brownsburg, Indiana, serving the broader Indianapolis metro.

 

Their service menu spans roof replacement, repair, maintenance, siding, gutters, windows, skylights, and specialty systems including EPDM, TPO, metal, and flat roofing.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



ZoomInfo lists Indy Rooftops' corporate office at 4254 N Raceway Rd, Indianapolis, with an employee band of 11–50.

 **Confidence: low** — ZoomInfo bands at this size are notoriously sloppy and likely include 1099 sales reps. 

BuildZoom confirms named personnel including Brian Weddle, Cheryl Edens, and Mitchell Dotson, and notes the company holds a General Contractor license and three additional licenses through the Indianapolis license board.

 Revenue estimate: $2M–$5M ARR based on the 511-review volume at a plausible 15–20% review capture rate and typical residential ticket sizes. **Confidence: low.** No public financials or permit volume data found at this time.

No job postings for Indy Rooftops were found on Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter, or ZipRecruiter in the last 30 days. The absence of active hiring ads suggests either a stable headcount or growth being handled through 1099/sales commission structures rather than W-2 adds. Worth re-checking next cycle — a company posting 62 reviews in 30 days is operationally busy, and that volume typically precedes a hiring push. No marketing, sales director, or ops leadership roles detected. Flag as neutral, not clean.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Yelp lists Indy Rooftops at 4254 N Raceway Rd, Indianapolis, IN 46234, with 42 reviews and 331 photos.

 Yelp rating was not explicitly published in results, but 42 reviews against 511 on Google is a significant funnel gap — they are almost certainly directing customers to Google exclusively, which is standard review-funneling behavior. 

They have been BBB Accredited since January 27, 2023,

 

and hold an A+ BBB rating.

 

Their Facebook page (facebook.com/IndyRooftops) shows 1,964 likes and 313 people "talking about this,"

 which is abnormally high engagement relative to their page size — suggesting either active paid promotion or viral organic posts, likely job/storm-chasing content. 

They promote a veteran discount on their contact page,

 a soft community signal that plays well in Nextdoor. No Facebook Ad Library data surfaced, so paid social posture is unconfirmed for this cycle. 

Reviews on HomeAdvisor/Angi mention a referral program explicitly,

 which is a deliberate volume driver worth noting.

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

indyrooftops.com was registered/first indexed with a metadata age of July 2022, putting their domain at roughly 3 years old — young for competitive local SEO. 

Their site copy leans on Indianapolis climate and code knowledge as an on-page differentiator,

They actively cross-reference Yelp, Angie's List, and BBB on their homepage,

 If Raptor doesn't have a structured, named referral mechanism with a defined incentive and a post-job trigger sequence, this is money being left on the table every week.

Raptor should build and index dedicated pages for Carmel, Fishers, Greenwood, Zionsville, and Noblesville with local FAQ schema now — both for organic rank and to establish AEO citations in generative engines before Indy Rooftops closes that gap.

---

## 1. Who They Are



Cox Roofing, also known as Cox Residential, is a family-owned roofing contractor based in Zionsville, Indiana, founded in 2012 and established as a trusted provider of roofing solutions in the Indianapolis area.

 

The company is family-owned, minority-owned, and women-owned, with locations across three states — Indiana, Kentucky, and Colorado.

 

They hold Owens Corning Platinum Preferred contractor status and an A+ BBB rating

, and they have diversified well beyond shingles into siding, gutters, painting, drywall, commercial, and multi-family — making them one of the broader-scope exterior contractors in the Indy market.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



With a workforce of 11 to 50 employees, the company emphasizes quality workmanship and exceptional customer service.

 **Confidence: medium** (sourced from [Inven.ai company profile](https://www.inven.ai/company-lists/top-20-roofing-companies-in-indiana); LinkedIn does not surface a precise headcount).

, which loosely corroborates the lower end of the 11–50 band. 

BBB lists Cox Roofing at 3 locations.

 **Confidence: medium.** Revenue estimate: at 508 Google reviews over roughly 12 years of operation, with multi-state coverage and a diversified service mix, a rough estimate of $5M–$10M annual revenue is reasonable for an operation this size — but no public filing or ZoomInfo record was found to pin it tighter. **Confidence: low.**

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



Cox Roofing currently has 22 open jobs listed on Indeed.

 That is an abnormally high open-role count for a sub-50-person company — a signal of either aggressive expansion or high turnover. 

A self-described Chief Operating Officer at Cox Roofing posted on LinkedIn about building out a dedicated supplement department

, which indicates they are investing in insurance claim maximization infrastructure — a direct revenue play. No discrete marketing director or CMO-level post was found in the last 30 days, but the volume of open roles suggests active ops and field-level hiring. The COO's stated mission — 

"to be the top Exterior Restoration contractor in the nation by 2030"

 — is worth flagging as an ambition signal.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Cox Roofing's Yelp listing is registered at 10837 Andrade Dr, Zionsville, IN 46077, with 24 photos

 — a thin photo presence for a company with 508 Google reviews, and no visible star rating surfaced in search snippets, which typically means very few Yelp reviews. That gap (500+ Google reviews, almost no Yelp traction) is a textbook review-funneling pattern — they almost certainly direct customers straight to Google and do not work the Yelp funnel. 

Their Facebook page (Cox Roofing, Zionsville) has 2,864 likes and 17 people currently talking about it

 — decent follower count but minimal active engagement. Notably, 

they introduced a persona called "IVO" on Facebook — described as "your roofing expert at Cox Roofing" — positioned to deliver tips, insights, and educational content.

 This is an AI-character or mascot content play worth watching. 

Cox Roofing has been BBB Accredited since April 14, 2017

, with the A+ rating intact. No Facebook Ad Library data surfaced in results, suggesting either no active paid social or minimal spend there.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Cox Roofing operates [coxroofingsystems.com](https://coxroofingsystems.com) and a legacy domain [coxres.com](https://coxres.com), which creates a split-authority problem — backlinks and indexing are likely fragmented across two root domains. 

Their Indianapolis service-area page claims service since 2013 and Owens Corning Platinum Preferred status

, which is solid schema fodder, but the page itself is thin on content depth. They have built out geo-targeted service-area pages (Indianapolis, Zionsville, etc.) and category pages for commercial, multi-family, and residential, which is a correct structural approach. 

Third-party sites like Cedur.com are citing Cox Roofing in "best roofers in Indiana" roundup articles

, which generates referral backlinks — a meaningful AEO and DR signal. The dual-domain architecture and lack of deep blog content are the most exploitable weaknesses from Raptor's perspective.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Based on available search results, Cox Roofing is being cited by name in third-party editorial roundups that generative engines pull from. Specifically, 

Inven.ai's "Top 20 Roofing Companies in Indiana" names Cox Roofing explicitly, describing their full service mix

 — and that type of structured list is exactly what ChatGPT and Gemini cite when answering "best roofers Indianapolis" queries. 

Cedur.com also names Cox Roofing in their Indiana best-roofers editorial

, another AI-readable citation source. Cox does not appear to have published any AEO-specific content (FAQ schema, Q&A pages, structured "how to choose a roofer" guides) on their own domain, meaning their AI visibility is dependent on third-party lists rather than owned content — a fragile position that Raptor can undercut by building stronger first-party AEO content.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Cox beats Raptor:** Sheer review volume — 508 reviews vs. Raptor's 673, but the gap is closing and Cox has broader brand recognition from 12+ years in market. Their three-state footprint, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred status, and multi-family/commercial verticals give them a wider revenue surface and more referral entry points than a residential-only operator. The "IVO" mascot/AI persona on social is a differentiated content play Raptor has not matched. Their 0.95 owner response rate is strong but Raptor's 5.0 star rating at comparable volume is a harder number to argue with.

**Where Raptor beats Cox:** Rating is unambiguous — 5.0 vs. 4.8 at scale. Raptor's review velocity (5 in 7 days vs. Cox's 9 in 30 days) is meaningfully faster right now, meaning Raptor is pulling away in recency signals that Google's local algorithm weights heavily. The most exploitable weakness: **Cox's dual-domain SEO architecture and near-zero Yelp presence indicate an underdeveloped digital infrastructure that a focused AEO and off-Google reputation push from Raptor could outflank quickly.**

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **The "IVO" persona / educational content character.** 

Cox introduced a named roofing expert persona on Facebook to deliver tips and insights.

 Whether this is AI-generated or a real person-branded approach, it creates a content engine that builds algorithmic trust. Cameron should consider a parallel play — a named, credentialed voice (human or brand persona) producing short-form educational content that feeds both social and AEO citation pools.

If Raptor holds or can pursue comparable manufacturer certification, deploying it above the fold on geo-targeted pages is a proven trust trigger that also feeds AI-answer citations.

3. **Multi-family and commercial as a review-volume accelerator.** 

Cox provides comprehensive multi-family roofing services across Indiana and Colorado.

 Commercial and multi-family jobs generate reviews from property managers who are often repeat clients and prolific reviewers. If Raptor is not actively soliciting reviews from any commercial work, that segment is an untapped review-volume lever worth pursuing.

 Critically,

Erie's post-acquisition integration noise is also likely suppressing any new AEO content investment at the local level right now.

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Erie beats Raptor:** National brand recognition, a lifetime warranty product, third-party financing at scale, and a $609M revenue machine that can spend on paid media without flinching. Their workaterie.com recruitment engine and Sales MIT program means they can flood local markets with commission-driven reps quickly.

**Where Raptor beats Erie:** Raptor holds a 5.0 star rating at 673 reviews vs Erie's 4.6 at 277 with zero recent review velocity — a dead signal in Google's local algorithm. Erie's subcontractor installation model is its most exploitable weakness:

Set a Google Alerts cadence for "Erie Home Indianapolis" and "Leaf Home Indianapolis" and be ready to surge Raptor's local paid media when Erie's GBP rating starts slipping.

## 2. Tactic of the Week

### Implement RoofingContractor + FAQPage Schema on Every Suburb Service Page — Today

**The WHY**

AI engines — Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, ChatGPT with Browse — do not guess at what your business does or where it operates. 

Schema markup tells Google and AI systems exactly what your business is in machine-readable code. Without it, search engines and AI tools have to infer your business type from content — and they sometimes get it wrong or simply skip you.

 For Raptor, "skipping" is the operative word: zero named citations in the six AI-style queries tested this week. The structural reason is almost certainly missing or incomplete structured data combined with a thin review count. Schema is the half you can fix in 48 hours.



The critical schema types for roofers are: `LocalBusiness`/`RoofingContractor` on the homepage, `Service` on service pages, `Review`/`AggregateRating` on review sections, and `FAQPage` on FAQ sections. Benefits include improved search result appearance via rich snippets, better local search rankings, and increased AI citation likelihood.





Clear NAP and hours in schema reduce mismatches and help map visibility. As answer engines pull factual data directly, structured data boosts your chances of being cited or synthesized in AI responses.

 That last sentence is the AEO mechanism: AI Overviews and Perplexity pull from structured, parseable data when composing contractor recommendations. Raptor is invisible to that pull right now.

**The HOW — five steps, execute by Friday**

1. Audit current schema state. Open [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) and run raptorroofing.com's homepage and two suburb service pages (e.g., Carmel, Fishers). Screenshot the output for baseline. Expected finding: missing or incomplete `AggregateRating` and `FAQPage` blocks.

2. Build a master JSON-LD block for the homepage using the `RoofingContractor` type. Include `name`, `url`, `telephone`, `address` with full Indianapolis metro `areaServed` array (Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, Westfield, Zionsville, Avon, Plainfield), `aggregateRating` pulling your current Google review count and star average, and `sameAs` links to GBP, BBB, and Yelp. Use the [Merkle Schema Markup Generator](https://technicalseo.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/) for the JSON-LD template. 

Prefer `RoofingContractor` over the generic `LocalBusiness` type when applicable.



3. Build a `Service` schema block for each suburb service page. 

Map one service page to one Service schema — do not cram everything into a single block.

 Each page gets `serviceType` ("Roof Replacement"), `areaServed` (specific suburb), and `provider` linked back to the root `RoofingContractor` entity.

4. Add `FAQPage` schema to each service page. Write three to five questions that reflect real search intent: "How much does a roof replacement cost in Carmel Indiana?", "Does homeowner's insurance cover hail damage in Noblesville?", "How long does a roof replacement take?". These questions feed directly into the AI Overview answer format. 

FAQPage schema increases AI citation likelihood

 because answer engines extract FAQ blocks as pre-formed Q&A pairs.

5. Validate every page with [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) and [Schema.org Validator](https://validator.schema.org/) before pushing to production. 

Test after publishing using Google's Rich Results Test or Schema Validator to check for errors — broken schema provides no benefit.



**The SUCCESS METRIC — measure at 30 days**

You are looking for: (1) zero schema errors on the five highest-traffic service pages, (2) FAQ rich snippet impressions appearing in the Performance report for suburb-level queries, and (3) a baseline AEO check — re-run the six queries from Section 3 manually in Google (AI Overview), Perplexity, and Bing Copilot and record whether Raptor is now named. ## 3. Raptor's AEO Standing

Six queries were tested against Google AI Overviews, Perplexity-style roundup pages, and third-party "best of" lists that AI engines demonstrably draw from. The results are consistent and unambiguous.
